subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should sandbox browser support be added as narrow external CDP/noVNC config, or should it wait for a broader browser backend/plugin interface?
rationale: The request adds new configuration and changes browser-control security boundaries, while project guidance favors core seams or plugin APIs over one-off core behavior when optional capability can be generalized.

options.title: Design Browser Backend Contract
options.body: Use the broader browser backend/plugin interface as the canonical direction, with external CDP/noVNC as one implementation of that contract.

options.title: Add External Endpoint Mode
options.body: Accept a narrow core config surface for externally managed CDP/noVNC endpoints with security review, docs, redaction, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Defer Core Change
options.body: Keep Docker-managed sandbox browser as the only supported sandbox browser path until maintainers confirm demand or a plugin API gap.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Backend Contract
recommendation.body: Use the broader browser backend/plugin interface as the canonical direction, with external CDP/noVNC as one implementation of that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across sandbox browser, config hardening, docs, and product-boundary decisions adjacent to this request.
